title: Open Food Log v0: meal
description: One meal or snack: what the person said they ate, the food each item was matched to, how much, what it held, and where the record came from. v0.1; may change until v1.

id.description: Assigned by the server that stores the meal.

eaten_at.description: When it was eaten, with an offset.

date.description: The person's local day, for a meal logged without a time. With eaten_at as well, it must be eaten_at's day in the person's time zone.

timezone.description: The person's IANA time zone when they ate (America/Chicago), beside eaten_at's offset, so a reader can tell which local day the meal belongs to and keep it there across daylight-saving changes.

logged_at.description: When the meal was recorded, with an offset, which may be long after eaten_at (a lunch logged that evening).

label.description: The person's own name for the occasion (pre-workout, second breakfast, iftar), beside or instead of meal_type. A reader that groups by the four meal types puts a meal with only a label under its own heading or with snacks.

recorded_by.description: Who recorded it: the person who ate it, a professional on their behalf (a dietitian, a coach, a clinic), or an app on its own (a smart scale, a meal service). Absent means the person.

media.description: Photos or other media of the meal that the producer keeps. OFL carries references, never the media itself; a producer that doesn't keep them leaves this out.

url.description: Where the producer serves it; it may need the producer's authorization.

updated_at.description: When the stored record last changed, by the server's clock. For mirroring; absent from a document that was never stored.

estimates.description: JSON pointers (RFC 6901) to values that were inferred or assumed rather than given: a size the person didn't say, a weight read from a photo, a food's numbers a model guessed.

source.description: Provenance: where the record came from. The same shape as an Open Workout Schema workout's.

client.description: The client or app, e.g. claude, myfitnesspal, cronometer.

external_id.description: The meal's ID in the app it came from.

id.description: Assigned by the server; used to edit the item.

text.description: What the person called it, in their words.

grams.description: The amount as a weight, worked out from amount and the food's portions, density or label (section 6 of the spec); with share, this person's part of it. Absent when the amount can't be weighed (a drink known only per 100 ml, a supplement).

share.description: For a dish shared with others: the part of amount this person ate (0.25 for a quarter of a pizza). grams and nutrients are already this person's part, amount × share.

nutrients.description: What this item held, as counted when it was logged. It does not change when the food's record later does. A key left out is unknown, never zero.

confidence.description: How sure the producer is of the item as recorded (its food and amount), 0 to 1, as a photo or a model reports it. It doesn't replace estimates, and two producers' confidences can't be compared.

food.description: The food an item was matched to. catalogue and custom are confirmed (custom covers the person's own foods and recipes); close and unmatched need the person to confirm; none means there is nothing to match, because the person gave the numbers themselves ('about 600 calories').

id.description: A food ID (ofc:, gtin:, usr:, recipe: or another namespace); null when nothing matched.

amount.description: How much, in the measure the person used.

unit.description: serving is the food's declared serving (label.serving) or a recipe's serving (yield_g / servings).

portion.description: With unit portion: the id of one of the food's portions.
